dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes by more than a factor of two between TESS sectors and between individual transits, with the signal dominated by two unusually deep events. Stable planet transits should look the same each orbit, so the pattern is best explained by systematics, variability or a blend rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth is not steady within the same SPOC source and varies by ~210% sector-to-sector, inconsistent with a transiting planet on the target. At minimum it implies a pipeline-dependent systematic/blend; at minimum it means folding sectors with 15204 ppm transits together with 960 ppm non-detections spuriously creates the 5718 ppm folded dip.
reasons.value: verdict: changes_within_a_source, p_constant: 1.048e-14, depths_S14=15204 ppm, S21=1539 ppm, S48=960 ppm, S75=9395 ppm

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent and the entire folded signal is carried by two anomalously deep events (top 3 share 0.97). Indicates the dip is made from a few bad events rather than a coherent planet.

reasons.why: Low planet-likelihood score supports false-positive interpretation, even though shape looks flat (-3.386 V-sigma) and odd_even.secondary are planet-like.
No on-target centroid confirmation to counter the depth variability; neighbours allow a blended solution and plausible non-target explanation remains.
reasons.value: verdict: inconclusive, why: no sector with a clear difference image
